label: The stance cannot meet its demand for reasons why and accept the fact with no reason
paraphrase: Stronger conclusion of the parity argument: in any picture and at any world, the stance does not at once meet its demand for reasons why, accept the fact o, and have o without a reason there, whether o is contingent or necessary. It binds both sides: a naturalist who requires a reason why God exists cannot accept an unreasoned contingent foundation, and a theist who requires a reason why contingent existents obtain cannot accept an unreasoned God, each under its own P1-P3 (parity map). A necessary fact with no reason is unreasoned, not brute (DISAMB-BRUTE-TERMINAL-UNREASONED). It is a consistency verdict on the stance; it does not say o has a reason, and it does not establish B2.
